alerts.title: Significant Weight Gain with Emerging Metabolic Dysregulation on DTG-Based ART
alerts.message: Guidelines state that weight gain should be discussed when starting ART and that proactive diet and exercise advice should be given to patients starting or switching ART, as obesity is an increasing problem in HIV care, particularly in women. Since switching to TLD 18 months ago, weight rose from 65 kg to 82 kg (BMI 25.6 to 32.4), waist circumference is 96 cm, and acanthosis nigricans is present, with fasting glucose 118 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.1%, now in the pre-diabetic range, alongside dyslipidaemia (LDL 148, HDL 38, triglycerides 212). Family history of T2DM is significant. Dolutegravir-associated weight gain is plausible, but the EFV-to-DTG switch coincides with this trend, and non-drug drivers (diet, activity, family history) are also likely contributors; the ART regimen cannot be attributed as the sole cause from these data. Guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months in the first year after DTG transition, which the excerpts support as a monitoring requirement.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide diet and exercise counselling now, arrange glucose monitoring every 3 months, and screen for and manage dyslipidaemia and hypertension (BP 138/88); reassess ART choice only if weight gain and metabolic changes persist despite lifestyle intervention.
